summary:
Option (b) is built as designed. The UI change is small and correct. OnCancel starts a nullable Stopwatch (MainWindow.xaml.cs:238). The existing 250 ms tick shows the line through ShowStopping, which uses only the clock (:242-247). EndStopping sits in StartScan's single finally, before ScanningPanel collapses (:170). Because of that order, the hook's `returned` stamp would catch a line that was never cleared. The wording is a pure function (StoppingWait.cs) whose boundaries are pinned by StoppingWaitTests. The Scanner, SynchronousIoCancel and the store were not touched.

The rig was extracted unchanged. I diffed StallingFileStore against f3c3dfa and found no difference. It now follows the accepted M1: a named-mutex RigLock, plus a sweep of leftover mappings filtered by a strict regex (\\127.0.0.1\fsa + 8 hex). Every departure from the design is declared.

What I ran:
- Build: 0 warnings, 0 errors.
- Default suite: 149/149 passed.
- Fitness: 25 rules, all hold.
- StallRig: builds; with bad arguments it exits 2.
- WindowCases.ps1 -Case C-006: passed (returned 15 ms after Cancel, detail `-`, final line written).
- WindowCases.ps1 -Case All: all 15 default cases passed. N-001 to N-004 were reported NOT RUN, exit 0.
- The abandon-rule regexes against samples: `_scanTask.WaitAsync`, the Task.Run chain and the WhenAny line all match. `running.WaitAsync(token)` and the scan's StartNew line do not.

What I did not run: N-001 to N-004 and the SMB-LOOPBACK StalledShareTests. They create and remove SMB client mappings on this machine. So the only positive proof that the wait line appears, counts up, keeps the UI live and clears through the real app is still owed to validate, as the design assigns. I read those cases and they feed their shapes.

One minor finding: O-008 is recorded as discharged, but only its cancelled-cleanly shape has a test. The faulted and finished-on-its-own shapes are fed by nothing. They rest on the single finally, and no seam can produce them without breaking the SL-033 no-test-seam rule.

There is no loop: this is one build attempt, caused by nothing.

findings.claim: O-008 (material case 'scan ends while the Stopping state is showing': cancelled cleanly, faulted, or finished on its own before the cancel took effect) is recorded as discharged, but only one of its three shapes has a test. (1) Cancelled cleanly: in the default run, C-006's scan returns 12-15 ms after Cancel, so the line is never on screen and EndStopping never has a shown line to clear there. The clear is only proved by N-001, which has never run. (2) Faulted: no test feeds it. (3) Finished on its own after Cancel: no test feeds it. Nothing is wrong in the code: EndStopping is in the one finally that every outcome passes through (MainWindow.xaml.cs:167-177). But the ledger says 'discharged' for two shapes nobody fed. A later review will read that as checked.
findings.evidence: src/FsAnalyser.App/MainWindow.xaml.cs:156-177 (catch ArgumentException / catch Exception / finally with EndStopping). tests/window/WindowCases.ps1 has no case that faults the scan or lets it finish after the hook presses Cancel. C-006 run here logged 'returned ms=15 ... detail=-'. The builder's own O-008 text says 'Not fed by any test: the faulted and finished-on-its-own paths'. .taad/fitness.yaml rule 'the shipped app carries no test seam' rules out a seam in src to produce them.
findings.fix: Re-dispose O-008's faulted and finished-on-its-own shapes as deferred. Reason: the shipped exe has no seam, the SL-033 rule forbids one, and they rest on the single finally. Leave the cancelled-cleanly shape owed to validate's N-001 run. No code change.

obligations.evidence: Owed to validate-slice, not to build. docs/design/SL-020-scanner.md now documents the person's 3x3 real-disconnect protocol, with a timed Close per mode. No real disconnect has been measured, and none can be from here.

src/FsAnalyser.App/StoppingWait.cs:31-33 gives no frequency and no upper bound: 'can take a minute or more' below 90 s, and no estimate from 90 s. StoppingWaitTests.TheTextIsAsciiAndGivesNoBoundOnTheWait checks, every 500 ms from 2 to 200 s, that the text contains no 'usually', 'about a minute' or 'remaining'. It passed in the 149/149 run.

tests/window/WindowCases.ps1 Test-C006 (SL-038 block) checks: exactly one `returned` line under 2000 ms, a final line, detail `-` on every stopping line, and title 'Stopping...'. Run here: passed, returned ms=15. The -Case All run also passed.

Test-N001 / CheckWaitLine in tests/window/WindowCases.ps1 feed the shape. FSA_HOOK_ARMED is the rig's marker and FSA_HOOK_CANCEL_DELAY_MS=3000, asserted as sincearmed 3000-4000. The first detail must appear 1900-3000 ms after Cancel, N must never go down, and there must be no gap over 1 s. It has never been executed: it changes SMB mappings, so I did not run it and neither did build. Only the analysis logic was checked, against synthetic logs in a scratch script that is not in the repo.

Test-N001 asserts that the returned detail is `-` and the final detail is `-`, exit 0, a report written, core.status Cancelled and an OutcomeTitle starting 'Stopped: '. It prints Cancel-to-return without asserting it. Never executed, for the same reason as O-004.

tests/FsAnalyser.Core.Tests/StoppingWaitTests.cs has a Theory at -5000, -1, 0, 1999, 2000, 89999, 90000 and 3600000 ms, plus one-tick checks either side of 2 s and 90 s, TimeSpan.MinValue, flooring and ASCII. The file is linked into Core.Tests.csproj. Ran 149/149 here.

Test-N002 runs two shapes, each on a fresh rig in interactive mode: Cancel at 3000 ms then Close at 5500 ms, and Close at 3000 ms with no Cancel. CheckCloseEscape asserts the window is gone within 1000 ms (hook clock, Window.Closed) and the process within 5000 ms (ExitTime against the close's UTC stamp). The case is written and feeds both shapes, but it has never run against the rig.

Only the cancelled-cleanly shape is fed. In the default run that is C-006, whose 15 ms return means no line was ever shown to clear; N-001 has not run. The faulted and finished-on-its-own shapes have no test (see finding m1). EndStopping in the single finally at MainWindow.xaml.cs:170 is structurally correct for all three. The existing throw and stop cases (C-012, O-016, C-006) pass with the hook's new timer, as the design required: I ran -Case All and all passed.

Replaced per M1 by Test-N003 (a second run with --wait-sec 2 exits 1 saying 'Another stall-rig run'; a third run waits; the first run's mapping survives) and Test-N004 (a killed run's leftover is swept by the next run). Both are written, both feed the shape, neither has run. The lock half is proved in the default run by SmbRigTests.ASecondRunWaitsForTheFirst and ALiveHolderFailsTheNextRunLoudlyAndAKilledOneDoesNotBlockIt: a cross-process holder is killed with Process.Kill, and the waiting run gets the lock. Both passed here.

tests/FsAnalyser.Core.Tests/Rig/SmbRig.cs: RigLock.Take(Local\FsAnalyser-SmbRig) is taken before anything else in the LoopbackShare constructor (:51) and released last in Dispose (:129). The sweep (:83-90) removes only paths that match ^\\127\.0\.0\.1\fsa[0-9a-fA-F]{8}$, and SmbRigTests.OnlyTheRigsOwnMappingsAreSwept pins that, including \\100.109.48.75\collab -> false. tests/window/StallRig/Program.cs:15-16 drops 'or on kill'.

.taad/fitness.yaml has three entries for 'only the rig changes the machine's SMB mappings', over tests/**/*.cs, tests/**/*.ps1 and eng/**/*.ps1. They carry the New/Remove-SmbMapping, New-SmbGlobalMapping, net use and WNet(Add|Cancel)Connection patterns, and SmbRig.cs is the only exception. Fitness check passes. A grep finds these cmdlets only in SmbRig.cs, plus one doc comment in StalledShareTests.cs:15.

.taad/fitness.yaml 'Cancel does not abandon the scan thread' now reads '[Ss]can\w*\.WaitAsync\(' (no leading \b), '\bScan\(.*\.WaitAsync\(' and 'Task\.WhenAny\(.*[Ss]can'. Tested here: `_scanTask.WaitAsync(ct)`, the Task.Run(...Scanner.Scan...).WaitAsync chain and the WhenAny line all match. `running.WaitAsync(token)` (MainWindow.xaml.cs:199) and the StartNew line do not.

tests/window/FsaWindowHook/StartupHook.cs:111-130: Delay() leaves an unset variable null, and DriveArmed only presses Cancel `if (cancelDelay is int cancelAt)` (:204). Armed stop with no cancel delay is refused (:119). WindowCases.ps1 sets FSA_HOOK_CANCEL_DELAY_MS='3000' explicitly for N-001 and for N-002 shape one, and leaves it unset for shape two.

StartupHook.cs:321-344: the final `stopping ... final=True` line comes from Dispatcher.ShutdownStarted, and the `returned` line from ScanningPanel's VisibilityProperty value-changed listener, attached before Cancel is raised. C-006 run here logged 'returned ms=15 ... detail=-' and then 'stopping ms=66 ... final=True', and asserted both.

CheckWaitLine in WindowCases.ps1 builds $times = 0 + tick ms + return ms and asserts $worst -le 1000. The hook timer is a DispatcherTimer on app.Dispatcher at Background priority, the same priority as the app's tick. 'The default run proves only that the line does not appear' appears in the WindowCases.ps1 header, the C-006 comment and SL-020-scanner.md. The assertion exists but has not run.

docs/design/SL-020-scanner.md, 'What is not measured': it says 'Closing the window quits at once' rests on the rig only, and the protocol adds one timed Close per mode (window gone, then Get-Process no longer lists the app).

cases.evidence: Test-C006 builds a large local tree (30,150 folders) and has the hook press Cancel in stop mode. Run here: returned 15 ms after Cancel, every stopping line shows detail `-`, final line written. At 15 ms the check cannot fail through the 2 s gate, because EndStopping runs before any tick. The gate itself is pinned by StoppingWaitTests. This is the negative check the design specifies.

Test-N001 starts StallRig (the server stops answering at the listing of hung and writes the marker), launches the app on the UNC root with FSA_HOOK_ARMED and FSA_HOOK_CANCEL_DELAY_MS=3000, and asserts sincearmed 3000-4000 ms. So it feeds the shape. It has never been executed: it is opt-in (-IncludeNetwork), changes SMB mappings, and is owed to validate.

The same Test-N001 run waits up to 150 s for the app to exit after the SMB client gives up. It asserts returned detail `-`, final detail `-`, exit 0, a report written, Cancelled and 'Stopped: '. Never executed.

StoppingWaitTests.TheWordingAtEachBoundary feeds -5000, -1, 0, 1999, 2000, 89999, 90000 and 3600000 ms. TheGateIsExactlyTwoSeconds feeds 2 s and 90 s plus or minus one tick. ANegativeSpanShowsNothing feeds MinValue. The file is linked from src/FsAnalyser.App/StoppingWait.cs. Ran in the default suite, 149/149.

Test-N002 feeds both shapes on a fresh rig each: Cancel at +3000 then Close at +5500 (asserting the wait line was on screen at the close), and Close at +3000 with no Cancel (asserting nothing pressed Cancel). Never executed against the rig. The builder rehearsed armed close only on a local tree, in a scratch script.

Only 'cancelled cleanly' is fed. In the default run that is C-006 at 15 ms, before any line could show; the opt-in case is N-001, which has not run. No test faults the scan after Cancel, and none lets it finish on its own after Cancel. See finding m1.

Replaced per the accepted M1. Test-N003 feeds 'a live run's fsa<8hex> mapping already exists' (an impatient run and a waiting run; the first run's mapping must survive). Test-N004 feeds 'a killed run's leftover mapping exists' (the next run sweeps it). Neither has run. In the default run, SmbRigTests exercises the lock across threads and across processes, including a killed holder.

Non-material and untested, and the reason still holds. _stoppingClock is set only in OnCancel (MainWindow.xaml.cs:238) and cleared in StartScan's finally (:170). CancelButton lives in ScanningPanel, which is collapsed after that finally. It has no IsCancel or access key (MainWindow.xaml:27-28). OnClosing calls _cancel?.Cancel(), not OnCancel. So no clock survives into the next scan.
Non-material, and the reason still holds: neither StoppingWait.For nor ShowStopping branches on drive type, and no DriveType or UNC detection was added.

Non-material, and the reason still holds: StartStoppingLog runs inside Act on the UI thread. Its DispatcherTimer is created on app.Dispatcher, and Detail/Stopping read FindName results only in dispatcher callbacks (StartupHook.cs:321-357).
Deferred to the person (O-001, owed to validate). The reason still holds: the modes change the person's network state. SL-020-scanner.md records the protocol.

Non-material. There is no test in the repo, only the builder's scratch rehearsal. The reason still holds: the hook logs 'refused ... the rig's marker ... did not appear within 60 s, so the stall never armed' (StartupHook.cs:194-197), and CheckActed then fails the case loudly. The deadline is 60 s from hook load, not the case timeout (see drift).

drift: RigLock uses a `Local\` mutex name (tests/FsAnalyser.Core.Tests/Rig/SmbRig.cs:176), which is per sign-in session. The builder's account says 'machine-wide mutex', and the SmbRig.cs comments say 'one rig run at a time on this machine'. SL-020-scanner.md correctly says 'one mutex per sign-in session'. A rig run in another session would not be serialised. It would fail loudly at New-SmbMapping rather than sweep anything, because mappings are per logon session.

The hook's armed-marker deadline is a fixed 60 s from hook load (StartupHook.cs:57, 194), not 'the case timeout' the design's hook contract names. The outcome is the same: the hook refuses, logs why, and the case fails.

The hook's 250 ms stopping timer stops when the scan returns (StartupHook.cs:333), not 'until the window closes or the report is written' as the design's hook component says. This follows from the m4 change, which is declared only as to where the `returned` stamp comes from.
StallRig is built by a new Update-StallRig function in WindowCases.ps1 that mirrors Update-Hook, rather than 'through the existing Update-Hook path'. This is cosmetic.
